name: Ife

summary.text: Ile-Ife is the sacred city of the Yoruba, where tradition says the world was created. Between about 1000 and 1400 it produced the famous bronze and terracotta heads and paved its courtyards with potsherds. Its Ooni never ruled a large empire, but Yoruba kings, and the Obas of Benin, traced their crowns to Ife.

snapshots.title: The sacred city
snapshots.text: Ile-Ife grows into a city around its shrines, the centre from which Yoruba dynasties claim descent.

snapshots.title: Classical Ife
snapshots.text: Ife artists cast lifelike heads in copper alloy and terracotta. Glass beads made in the city are traded widely. Benin's royal line looks to Ife for its regalia.

links.label: Oyo's founder Oranmiyan came from Ife

snapshots.title: Ife in the wars
snapshots.text: In the 19th-century wars Ife is sacked (1849) and resettled (1854), and its quarrel with the Oyo refugee town of Modakeke begins.

today.text: The Ooni of Ife reigns at Ile-Ife, Osun State, and remains one of the most senior Yoruba kings.
today.title: Ooni of Ife

reviewNotes: Ife's political reach (as opposed to ritual reach) is not well known; influence is drawn small.
